query: A person hit me first and I hit back to protect myself. Is it a crime?

gold_references.label: Section 34
gold_references.role: things done in private defence are not offences

gold_references.label: Section 35
gold_references.role: right of private defence of body

acceptable_references.label: Section 37
acceptable_references.reason: restrictions on the right of private defence

required_points: Under Section 34, nothing done in the exercise of the right of private defence is an offence.
Section 35 provides every person the right to defend their own body against an offence affecting the human body.
The right is limited; it cannot extend beyond what is necessary for defence, and there must not be time to seek public authority protection (Section 37).
optional_points: Whether this specific situation qualifies depends on the nature of the attack, the force used in retaliation, and whether it was necessary.
forbidden_points: Hitting back to protect oneself is always a crime.
Private defence permits any degree of force in retaliation.

notes: Scenario query. Should identify private defence under Section 34/35 with proper caveats.
